text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:

- Swiss lower house of parliament rejects a referendum proposed by a group of young pro-EU activists for a renewed Swiss application to join the European Economic Area, which Swiss voters rejected in a 1992 referendum.
- The federation of Swiss regional banks reported a 12.8 percent drop in net profit to 126 million Swiss francs in 1996.
- The Swiss government decided not to free Switzerland's federal railroad company SBB from the value added tax.
- Switzerland plans to join a new European University Convention which requires member countries to recognise degrees granted by each other's universities.
- Swiss elevator and lift maker Schindler reported a 13 percent increase in net profit to 88.6 million Swiss francs in 1996.
Sales rose by 9.4 percent to 5.19 billion francs.

- The canton of Zurich plans to charge an annual high-school fee of 800 Swiss francs, the conservative majority in the cantonal parliament decided on Monday. Zurich voters will have to give final approval in a referendum later this year.
- Switzerland' s sport equipment sector will register a five percent increase in sales for the winter season 1996/97, according to IHA market researcher.
